concept.title: Finding your way around
concept.shortdesc: Inside a project, the page is framed by a narrow rail down the left and one top bar across the top, so the work itself gets the rest of the screen.

ul.li: The rail has a button for each part of the project — Define, Verify, Plan and Agents — and links to Activity and Settings. Click a group to open its pages beside the rail (Define holds Overview, Guided Definition, Requirements and Interviews, for example), then click the page. The group holding the page you are on is marked. The list closes when you arrive, or with Esc or a click anywhere else. Projects at the top of the rail returns to all projects in the workspace.

The top bar reads left to right: the workspace switcher, the project and the page you are on (click the project's name for its overview), the search across every project, Help, the notification bell and the account menu.

conbody.p: On a phone the top bar names where you are in two lines: the project, small, above the page you are reading. The project menu opens from ☰ in the top bar, and a row of tabs along the bottom reaches the pages used most on the move: Overview, Reqs (Requirements), V&V and Review. More opens the menu as a page of its own: the project at the top (tap it for all projects), the workspace switcher and the search, then each group of pages as a list under its name (tap the name to fold the group away), Help, and under You your account menu and the bell.
